# Suvaṇṇakakkaṭajātaka (Ja 389)
**ID:** Ja 389
**Section:** Jātaka (ja)

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Suvaṇṇakakkaṭajātaka* (Ja 389), known in English as *The Golden Crab*, is a tale preserved in the canonical Jātaka collection [SuttaCentral]. According to the narrative frame, the Buddha told this birth-story while residing at the Bamboo Grove (*Veḷuvana*) to commemorate the Elder Ānanda offering up his life for the Buddha's sake when confronted by the elephant Dhanapāla [SuttaCentral]. When the monks in the Hall of Truth discussed Ānanda’s self-sacrifice, the Buddha stated that Ānanda had also given up his life for him in past births, introducing the story with the opening words "Gold-clawed creature" [SuttaCentral]. The core narrative involves the Bodhisatta carrying a golden crab (*suvaṇṇakakkaṭaka* / *kañcanakakkaṭaka*) that comes to his aid against a snake and a crow [Fausböll 1883].
The Pali text is directly commented upon in the third volume of the *Jātaka-aṭṭhakathā*, sharing twelve matching passages identified by DharmaNexus (most notably segment range §3.4–5.3 aligning with commentary segments §2615–2621) [DharmaNexus; Fausböll 1883]. DharmaNexus also detects minor automated cross-language alignments with a Tibetan tantric text, the *Śrī-buddhakapāla-nāma-yoginī-tantrarājā* (D0424), though these reflect mechanical matches rather than established parallels [DharmaNexus]. Outside of textual transmission, episodes of the *Suvaṇṇakakkaṭajātaka* are known in Southeast Asian art and epigraphy, having been documented on Buddhist boundary markers (*sīmā* / *semā* stones) from the Khorat Plateau and Chi Valley culture in Northeast Thailand [Murphy; Skilling].
**Parallels and text reuse**

- Text reuse within the Pali corpus (DharmaNexus): Jātaka-aṭṭhakathā (Tatiyo bhāgo) (Atk S0513a3) (§3.4–5.3 ↔ §2615–2621)
- Cross-language matches (DharmaNexus): དཔལ་སངས་རྒྱས་ཐོད་པ་ཞེས་བྱ་བ་རྣལ་འབྱོར་མའི་རྒྱུད་ཀྱི་རྒྱལ་པོ། (śrī-buddhakapāla-nāma-yoginī-tantrarājā) (D0424) [bo]
